scope: Browser-visible Portfolio interactions on the exact publication bundle; this is a test inventory, not a claim of physical-device qualification.

assertions: Published route titles and internal links resolve
Atlas crosswalk destinations match
Research article and notebook links use the rendered reader surface
Legacy /reproduce/ redirect reaches the external catalog fixture
limits: Article and notebook route coverage is conditional on publication.json being served by the finished bundle; source-only runs exercise the local static routes.

assertions: Chapter hash updates and browser Back restore route
Finished-bundle article links and figure anchors check sticky-header clearance, Back/Forward route, hash and scroll restoration
Finished-bundle Pagefind search checks no-result, clear, result activation, Back/Forward and touch Close
Menu Escape closes and returns focus
Skip link focuses main
Source-served appearance audit checks Auto/light/dark selection and persistence
Menu opens from keyboard, moves focus into its links, supports Tab/Shift+Tab, and Escape restores trigger focus
Mobile menu and theme actions use touch at phone widths
Axe WCAG checks, responsive overflow and target dimensions run on source-served routes; finished-bundle interaction audit checks representative routes
Reduced-motion scroll behavior and forced-colors fallbacks
limits: The exact finished-bundle job does not run the complete appearance matrix or denied-storage audit; those checks are source-served only.

assertions: Native wheel/finger scroll moves the page without changing camera or replay
Sticky stage remains aligned across chapter scroll and releases at journey end
Chapter anchor navigation preserves history
Desktop browser zoom does not change graph camera
No engine request before explicit intent
Concurrent Start is deduplicated
Ignition counts 1.8 seconds of active-visible time
Started state survives session navigation and BFCache
Startup timeout, failed imports and context loss retain state and permit retry
Reduced-motion/no-script/WebGL failure keeps a usable static model
Keyboard and pointer replay state changes are checked
Inspector selection reports selected node and route counts
Camera controls preserve replay position and reset view
Touch gestures cover orbit, pinch, pan and replay scrubbing
Input selection and pointer text drag remain native without camera movement
Replay and lighting are deterministic over all 361 frames
Tab selection updates active pane
Exiting panes become inert and aria-hidden immediately and relocate focus
Reversal restores valid focusable tabs
DOM pane and GPU backing easing remain synchronized
Touch orbit preserves pane alignment
Deep zoom remains finite and reset returns framing
Reduced-motion context transitions, keyboard operation and axe checks
On the phone viewport, Arrow/Home/End focus changes update aria-pressed/detail selection; touch selects a connected milestone, its Read article link navigates, and Back returns to the selected map
Article links and Atlas destinations resolve
Anchor scrolling and sticky index are visually/layout checked
Finished articles expose executable cell/output structure and source revision
Evidence disclosures open/close by pointer and keyboard

On the finished MyST article, Playwright clicks Load browser Python, injects local asset failures, checks retry and duplicate-click behavior, then requires an attached browser kernel and executes a smoke cell or asserts a captured Pyodide network failure
Focused unit tests separately cover stubbed asset/kernel rejection and retry branches
limits: Actual MyST execution depends on Pyodide network availability in the CI browser; a network-block result is recorded as blocked runtime, not successful execution.

assertions: Finished bundle requires links and validates every article's PDF/DOCX/LaTeX/JATS exports
Playwright triggers actual PDF, Word, LaTeX ZIP and JATS XML downloads for a published article, checks the suggested filename, bytes and reader URL remains unchanged
limits: Playwright exercises one representative article's browser download events; CI validates generated bytes and links for every published article.

assertions: Publication tests verify notebook bytes, generated reader/download routes and cross-notebook links
Browser follows the real Open in JupyterLite link, checks the selected notebook path and compares rendered code cell count/source to its preserved .ipynb
Browser triggers a preserved .ipynb download and compares its SHA-256 to the publication manifest
limits: JupyterLite bootstrap and cell loading are exercised; this route does not edit or execute a JupyterLite cell or validate workspace persistence.

assertions: Exact compiled package link targets are checked in the article and evidence handoff
Article-to-catalog navigation and Back are exercised against a locally intercepted fixture
limits: The external catalog's actual package downloads/exports are not exercised; the test deliberately makes no live external transaction.
No test launches JupyterLite, runs a published notebook cell, or validates persistence of edits in that workspace.
Playwright Chromium emulation, injected WebGL loss, axe and synthetic touch do not substitute for physical-device, GPU-driver, or screen-reader testing.
Performance profile and score/byte budgets are maintained separately; they are not changed or conflated with deterministic interaction assertions.
